## Seat note for triage — evidence and constraints only. ⛔ Not graded, not labelled: routing and grading are triage's.

`domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `session_01CRJge11jso9TpXRWFt1Z49`, round 1. This card came out of #6595's dispatch as an out-of-scope finding; I verified it exists and read it, which is the PM's duty on `out_of_scope_findings`. Adding what I can add without stepping on triage.

### ⭐ Asking triage to look at this one early, and why

It is a **permission-widening path**, not a data-loss annoyance, and the card's own sharpest sentence is the reason: the button labelled **All** — which reads as "grant everything" — can **widen effective read access** by deleting a `readScope: own` narrowing. Nothing shows a diff and nothing errors. Both save doors persist the truncated row, and at package scope `mergePermissionSlice` takes in-scope rows entirely from `edited` by design, so `base` cannot restore what was dropped.

The asymmetry the card names is the part I would not want lost in grading: **the reviewing surface shows a value the authoring surface deletes on the next bulk click.** objectstack#4115 added the Export column and the scope cell precisely so a reviewer could see those keys.

⚠️ Stated honestly, so it is not over-graded either: this needs an admin acting in an admin tool, and the widening is a fall-back to default depth rather than an unauthenticated exposure. I am **not** claiming p0 — I am asking that it not sit in the ungraded pool on the assumption that it is an ordinary tidy-up, because the read of the title alone ("bulk buttons delete three keys") undersells it.

### ⛔ Serial constraint, recorded now so it is not re-derived

The fix lands in **`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx`**, which is the file **open PR #6607 (#6595) is currently changing**. This card is serialised behind that PR and ⛔ must not be dispatched alongside it.

Related but distinct, and both should stay separate: **#6606** (the permission authoring shapes are absent from `PAYLOAD_SHAPES` in `check-designer-field-key-parity.mjs`, so this whole defect class is invisible to that gate on the permission surface) is the *why nothing caught it* half.

### Note on the eventual fix

The card's suggested shape — merge rather than replace, starting from `{ ...cur }` and setting only the keys `OBJECT_ACTIONS` actually authors — matches what `updateObjectPerm` already does on the per-checkbox path, so this is one path converging on its sibling rather than a new convention. ⚠️ But whoever dispatches it should note that this touches **permission semantics**, which sits on this lane's recorded human floor: the `none` arm in particular ("clear the grants the matrix owns, not the row") is a behaviour decision about what an admin's "None" means, not a mechanical merge fix.

**Serial constraints cleared.** Triage serialised this behind #6595; **PR #6607 merged 2026-08-27T13:30Z**, so `PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx` is free. ⚠️ Triage's instruction stands: **re-take the surface on the merged ref** — #6607 removed the retired `allowRestore` / `allowPurge` columns from this very file, so the row-shape code has moved since this card was written. ⛔ `allowRestore` / `allowPurge` are retired and are NOT part of this card.

## ⛔⛔ The card's own suggested fix is WRONG on one arm — read this before you implement it

The card says: *"`none` needs the same treatment — clearing the grants the matrix owns, not the row."* **Do not do that**, unless your measurement overturns my reasoning below, in which case say so and your reading wins.

Reasoning: the defect is arms that **grant while silently dropping a narrowing**. `all` / `crud` / `read` set permissions and wipe `readScope` / `writeScope` / `allowExport` — that is the widening path, and the **All** button is its sharpest form (an admin clicking "grant everything" deletes a `readScope: own` narrowing with no diff and no error).

`none` grants nothing. Writing `{}` drops the narrowings too, but with no grants surviving there is nothing for a scope to widen — so **`none` is not part of the defect.** Applying merge semantics to it would leave `allowExport: true` (and the scopes) alive after a click on the button labelled **None**. ⭐ That is a permissive outcome **that does not exist today**, introduced by the fix, on a surface whose whole problem is silent permissiveness. It also sits on this lane's human floor: what an admin's "None" means is a behaviour decision, not a mechanical merge.

**So: fix `all` / `crud` / `read` by merging. ⛔ Leave `none` exactly as it is (replace with `{}`), and say in the PR body that you did and why.** If you conclude `none` genuinely must change to be coherent, ⛔ **do not pick** — report it as a fork with your measurement.

## PM mechanism assumptions — measure them; your reading wins

⛔ This card's line numbers and code block predate #6607. **Find constructs by name.**

1. I assert `OBJECT_ACTIONS` does **not** include `allowExport`, so `allowExport` is "shown in the preview but not authored by the matrix". The card says the preview renders all three keys and objectstack#4115 added the Export column for reviewers. ⚠️ **If `allowExport` IS in `OBJECT_ACTIONS`, my `none` reasoning above weakens** — a key the matrix authors is one it may legitimately clear. Measure this first; it is load-bearing for the fence.
2. `updateObjectPerm`'s per-checkbox path already spreads (`{ ...cur, [action]: value }`) and preserves the three keys. So this is **one path converging on its sibling**, not a new convention — verify that on the merged ref rather than trusting it.
3. Both save doors persist the truncated row, and at package scope `mergePermissionSlice` takes in-scope rows entirely from `edited` (ADR-0086 P0) so `base` cannot restore them. That is the card's claim for why this is not display-only; ⭐ it is also the reason a test that only checks editor state proves nothing — pin through the save path.

## ⭐ A root-cause hypothesis, offered as a hypothesis

`ObjectPerm` in `permission-slice.ts` is described as a **hand-written SUBSET** of the spec's `ObjectPermission`, with three declared keys modelled by neither it nor `OBJECT_ACTIONS`. ⭐ **That is the same "keys dropped by silence" shape PR #6618 fixed two hours ago in this very directory** — `FormFieldSpec.options` was the last hand-written element type in `form-spec.ts`, mirroring 3 of the spec's 5 keys and dropping 2 by silence; it now derives from the spec type with its narrowings named in an `Omit`, and the dropped key **says so**.

Whether the same derivation is right here is **yours to judge**, not mine to instruct — it may be larger than this card. But if it is cheap, it converts "the editor cannot model these keys" from a recurring bug source into a compile-time fact. ⛔ If it is not cheap, do the bounded fix and say so; do not widen this PR on my speculation.

## Verification bar

- ⭐ **Pin the round-trip, not the click**: a row carrying all three keys through each of the four buttons, observed **after the save path**, not in editor state.
- Include a pin for the **All** button specifically — it is the widening shape and the one a reader will look for.
- ⛔ `none` gets a pin too: that it still clears the row. That pin is the fence made mechanical, so a later refactor cannot quietly adopt the card's suggestion.
- A zero needs a positive control in the same query shape. Reverse-verify: predict the direction, prove the mutation on disk, prove the restore by observation (`git diff HEAD` empty **and** a hash match), never by exit code.

## Out of scope, named so it is not swept in

**#6606** — the permission authoring shapes are absent from `PAYLOAD_SHAPES` in `check-designer-field-key-parity.mjs`, which is *why nothing caught this*. Different lane (`domain:devx`), different card. ⛔ Do not touch the gate.

Deliver a **draft** PR with `Fixes #6605` only if all four arms are disposed of within the fence (three fixed, `none` deliberately unchanged and pinned). If anything is left open, use `Part of`.
